# Implicit Chain-of-Thought

> A reading list about reasoning without writing every intermediate step, with explanations, paper summaries, and downloadable citations.

This research is also discussed as latent reasoning or latent chain-of-thought.

Yuntian Deng and colleagues first proposed implicit chain-of-thought reasoning in [2023](https://arxiv.org/html/2311.01460v1#S2.SS3): training language models to reason through continuous hidden states rather than write out explicit intermediate steps. The paper's [distillation method](https://arxiv.org/html/2311.01460v1#S3) is one implementation of that proposal. Their [2024 work](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.14838) introduced step-by-step internalization.

## Using the data

Use the original papers for scientific claims. Summaries and categories are written for this reading list, not copied abstracts. Papers can belong to several categories. Coverage includes related generation methods and is not exhaustive.

- `id` identifies a paper; `paper_url` links to the original source; `record_url` links to an independently fetchable entry at `/papers/{id}/`. Earlier full-list anchors still work through `legacy_record_url`.
- Each entry has `json_url`, `markdown_url`, `bibtex_url`, and `csl_url`. Use the topic downloads or individual entries when you do not need the complete list.
- `author_names` preserves the authors' names and order.
- Optional `related_terms` provides editorial search terminology, such as latent reasoning or latent chain-of-thought. These terms are also visible on the paper's page; they do not replace its title or citation. Search them alongside the title and summary.
- Optional `method_comparisons` contains the comparisons shown on a paper's page, with the papers discussed in `source_ids`, primary-source links in `source_urls`, and readable `source_labels`. Each comparison identifies its topic guide. A comparison may explain a difference or a documented influence; its presence is not itself an influence claim.
- `added_at` is when a paper was added to this list, not its publication date. Tracking began {{ site.data.meta.addition_tracking_started_at }}; initial-collection records omit this field. Release history lists `added_papers` IDs. A new addition may be an older paper.
- `first_public` is the earliest public date we have verified, usually the first arXiv submission. An earlier conference presentation has a source note. It is not an independently verified announcement date.
- `citation_date` is the date of the linked source: the initial submission for an arXiv preprint, or the publication date for a DOI-only entry. The complete BibTeX and CSL-JSON files cite that source. Source URLs may serve revised versions.
- `publication` metadata describes a verified published version. For arXiv entries, its title, author list and year may differ; use `publication_bibtex_url` or `publication_csl_url` for that version. DOI-only entries use this metadata in their default citations too. Absence means we have not verified a publication record, not that the paper is unpublished.
- Optional `demos` link to interactive examples and model details. Each demo's `paper_relationships` distinguishes `implementation` from `related_method`; `relationship` gives its connection to the current paper. A related-method demo does not implement that paper. Topic downloads also list the demos shown in the guide. Demo outputs are examples, not benchmark evidence; use the method paper for scientific claims and cite the model separately when you use it.
- Release entries can list `updated_papers` (IDs and changed fields) and `removed_papers` (IDs). Refresh cached records using the current corpus; do not treat a historical release as the current membership list.
- `provenance` says where we first found a paper.
- Category IDs and filter values are defined in the category file; related terms are not necessarily synonyms.

## Research workflow

Choose the relevant topic, identify papers whose methods address the question, then read the original sources. The topic guides compare training and computation choices with source links. Verify the exact result, setting and limitations before citing it. Chronological order is not proof of influence, and citing a paper does not necessarily mean building on its method. Export a citation for the version actually used. This curated list is a starting point, not an exhaustive literature search.
